question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B=40^\circ\) and \(\angle C=60^\circ\). The bisector \(AD\) of \(\angle BAC\) intersects \(BC\) at \(D\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADC\) in degrees.

solutions.explanation: \(\angle BAC=80^\circ\), and \(\angle BAD=40^\circ\). Since \(\angle ADC\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle ABD\), \(\angle ADC=\angle B+\angle BAD=40^\circ+40^\circ=80^\circ\).
solutions.title: Triangle exterior-angle property
